title: Stored x-only leaf birthday search on secp256k1 at 125.364878449: six leaves per batched inverse, with LDADD cursor advances at both hops, mask-tested d3 buckets and a pointer-pair scan

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.3900001 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins, with no heuristic: the Chen-Stein method on cross-node leaf pairs bounds P(no collision), and drops, caps and the enumerated inline-carry sites of the kernels (section 3.4) are charged failure rows, while RNDR, the ideal coin source, adds none (section 6). On every run its total work is at most 2^125.364878449 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Each pair of generator points X, Y gives six leaves, the x-coordinates of phi^t(X) + Y and phi^t(X) - Y for t = 0, 1, 2, from one batched inverse of y_Y^2 - y_X^2, the product of their three denominators (section 3.1). Machine (section 2.1): 2^72 nodes, each with one processor (base AArch64 with FEAT_RNG and FEAT_LSE) and a memory below 2^64 bytes, whose links deliver a message's four words at the address its sender stored and keep no flags, rings or counters. Beyond its sender's instructions, every message's charge includes 8 instruction-equivalents at each hop: its delivery as route.s dlv (three LDPs of the message, two STPs at the address, RET: 6), which the experiment executes for every message of its 4 x 4 run, and its port's in-flight count (2). Hop 1, hop 2 and grouping are charged 18, 18.25 and 19.25 per record, the unrolled loops' control included; the senders advance their cursors with LDADD, hop 2 stores the slot end back on a drop, and the final cursors are clamped at the slot end. certificate.py gives at most 396.5534 instructions per leaf and the claim 125.364878449. Peak memory at most 2^135.9988 bytes; preprocessing at most 2^110.2061 units, included; no advice; certificate.py checks that the work, memory and preprocessing figures are the least 9-decimal (work) or 4-decimal (memory, preprocessing) values at or above their exact values, and that 0.3900001 is below the success bound. The bound is for the machine of section 2.1. Lineage: our b3716a20 (the six-leaf fwd and bwd kernels, the site table and the success argument, unchanged here), package 8f733826 (field rows, fe_inv, class row, a64.py) and submissions 3828873f, 6ef3e7b3, d637fb0a, 9798f5f4 and d9e3dbf4 (STADD, paired scan comparisons, prefix4, the generator and candidate allowances, a claim on a decimal grid); no prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the six-leaf kernels on production points, and the emit, both hops (each message delivered by executing dlv) and the grouping on a 4 x 4 machine, against exact references; check the arithmetic sites of section 3.4; compare the counts of the leaf, inversion, transport, delivery and grouping kernels with certificate.py; run the q25 toy with six leaves per incidence and certificate.py. Budget-limited parts run stated minimums. Not a production-scale attack.
